attacks.claim: The offline expiry check only catches a device clock set earlier than the download time. A clock wound back to just after download still shows a forecast past its valid_until in color, which breaks the 'never show an expired rating in color' rule.
attacks.evidence: 'if the device clock reads earlier than that, the stored forecast is treated as expired' and QA 'Device clock moved earlier than offline download time: Pass' (only tests the earlier-than-download direction)

attacks.claim: The artifact never says the CDN honors valid_until. A CDN TTL longer than valid_until would keep serving expired ratings in color even though the origin expires them correctly. At the stated 92% hit rate, most responses come from the CDN.
attacks.evidence: 'serves zone geometry + ratings from our CDN' and 'our API keeps serving forecasts still inside valid_until and expires them on time' with ABSENT: CDN TTL or valid_until-bound cache rule

attacks.claim: Rollback does not reach offline phones that cannot fetch remote config. The flag only takes effect on foreground and the stored forecast data is only deleted on that path, so stale colored ratings can persist in the field, which is the case the artifact says it prevents.
attacks.evidence: 'takes effect on next app foreground' and 'on-device forecast data stored with offline maps is deleted, so no stale ratings remain on phones'

attacks.claim: When a center asks to stop, removing it from config leaves its offline copies colored until valid_until, which can be days away. This conflicts with the center's request and the agreed rule that stale safety information is never shown as current.
attacks.evidence: 'any offline copies expire at their valid_until'

attacks.claim: The agreed rule requires ratings from issuing centers under a signed data agreement. The only agreement cited is with WADE, and the artifact itself implies centers can separately ask removal, so per-center rights are unverified. The blog post also has no attribution or link, and legal review (LGL-902) covered only card text and terms.
attacks.evidence: 'WADE data agreement signed 2026-09-30 (contract C-2209)' with ABSENT: per-center agreements; blog post 'Avalanche forecasts from 19 avalanche centers across the US and Canada, now in Ridgeline Maps. Free for everyone.' with 'Card text and the terms-of-use update were reviewed by legal (LGL-902)'

attacks.claim: The bbox parameter is not described as validated or bounded. Random bbox values give unique cache keys, so requests bypass the CDN and hit origin, which is capped at 6 instances. The per-IP limit does not stop a distributed attacker.
attacks.evidence: 'GET /avy/v1/zones?bbox=…' with 'CDN-cached responses are not counted' and 'origin autoscaling capped at 6 instances'

attacks.claim: No load or cache-miss-storm test is documented. Polls every 10 min can invalidate caches, and the origin cap of 6 instances is untested against 10-100x peaks, so 5xx errors are likely at the morning peak or during a storm.
attacks.evidence: 'Projected 1.8M zone requests/day at 92% CDN hit rate' and 'origin autoscaling capped at 6 instances' with ABSENT: load test results

attacks.claim: The bbox equals the visible map area. Combined with the IP address logged for rate limiting, server logs can build a location trail, even though the artifact says device location is not sent. No retention period is stated.
attacks.evidence: 'device location is not sent' versus 'GET /avy/v1/zones?bbox=…' and 'rate limited at origin to 120 req/min per IP' with ABSENT: log retention or bbox logging policy

attacks.claim: No alert covers the core invariant. Monitoring tracks poll success, per-center update age, 5xx, and CDN hit rate, but not expired forecasts being served or cached past valid_until. A 26 h per-center alert is also far slower than forecast expiry.
attacks.evidence: 'any center not updated for 26 h during its season' and monitoring list with ABSENT: served-expired-forecast metric or alert

attacks.claim: Expired forecasts and zones with no forecast both use gray hatched fill. The map does not distinguish them, so a user may read an expired zone as merely unknown.
attacks.evidence: 'gray hatched fill and "No current forecast"' and 'gray hatched with "Forecast expired [time]"'

attacks.claim: The VoiceOver/TalkBack spec only covers colored zones. Announcements for expired and no-forecast zones are not defined.
attacks.evidence: 'zone announced as "[zone], danger 3 Considerable, issued [time]"' with ABSENT: announcement for gray zones

attacks.claim: Showing the highest of three bands as the zone label and color may misstate the forecast for the zone. The agreement bars altering ratings, and the artifact does not show that this aggregation is permitted.
attacks.evidence: 'The zone color uses the highest of the three' with 'may not alter ratings or forecast text' and ABSENT: agreement language on aggregation

attacks.claim: The 92% CDN hit rate and 1.8M requests/day are unsourced projections that drive the cost math.
attacks.evidence: 'Projected 1.8M zone requests/day at 92% CDN hit rate'

attacks.claim: QA 'Pass' results do not specify how the 19-center comparison was done, and the blog render check at 10:00 is a manual step with no defined procedure.
attacks.evidence: 'match the center's own site for 3 consecutive days' and 'after a check that all 19 centers render'

attacks.claim: The $400/month CDN alert has no projected CDN cost behind it, so the threshold cannot be checked against the budget.
attacks.evidence: 'CDN budget alert at $400/month' with ABSENT: CDN cost projection

attacks.claim: Launch to 100% lands Monday Nov 23, the week before US Thanksgiving and at peak ski-season traffic, with no staffing or on-call plan stated.
attacks.evidence: 'Nov 23 08:00: flag on for 100%' with ABSENT: on-call staffing for launch week

attacks.claim: The layer depends on one upstream data feed (WADE) and an undisclosed CDN vendor. Exit is not described beyond removing centers.
attacks.evidence: 'using forecasts published by the regional avalanche centers in the Western Avalanche Data Exchange (WADE)' with ABSENT: fallback source or CDN exit plan

attacks.claim: The center list is duplicated by hand in the blog post and config, which invites drift.
attacks.evidence: 'list in config/avy_centers.json, same list in the blog post'

attacks.claim: Lens checks with no attack: ux-value, ux-efficiency, and cost-runaway (apart from the CDN note) were checked and show no gating problem.
attacks.evidence: 'Layer toggle: Map layers > Avalanche forecast. Free for all users, no account needed.'

attacks.claim: The offline expiry check only compares device time to the stored server download time. If the device clock is moved back to any point after download but before the real time, an expired forecast is still shown in color. This violates the agreed rule that the app must never present stale safety information as current.
attacks.evidence: "The app also stores the server time at download; if the device clock reads earlier than that, the stored forecast is treated as expired." QA only tests "Device clock moved earlier than offline download time".

attacks.claim: The kill switch cannot reach offline phones. The flag takes effect only on next foreground, and purge is tied to a flag fetch. An offline phone in the field keeps showing a wrong or withdrawn rating in color until valid_until. The artifact also says purge happens on "next app foreground" in one place and "next launch" in QA, which is inconsistent.
attacks.evidence: "Set `avalanche_layer=false` (remote config, takes effect on next app foreground)." and "`avalanche_layer=false`: layer hidden, offline forecast data purged on next launch" and "no stale ratings remain on phones."

attacks.claim: CDN caching has no TTL, and nothing states that cached responses cannot outlive a forecast's valid_until. The claim that expiry happens "on time" depends on the CDN respecting it, which the artifact does not show.
attacks.evidence: "serves zone geometry + ratings from our CDN" and "our API keeps serving forecasts still inside `valid_until` and expires them on time; nothing is extended." ABSENT: CDN TTL or cache-control policy.

attacks.claim: The core safety invariant has no monitoring. No dashboard metric or alert detects an expired forecast served in color, a zone colored from an out-of-window forecast, or a client-side expiry failure. Per-center alerting uses a 26 h threshold, which is longer than a typical forecast validity window.
attacks.evidence: "Dashboard: WADE poll success, last update per center, endpoint 5xx and p95, CDN hit rate, crash-free sessions on 6.12." and "any center not updated for 26 h during its season". ABSENT: any expired-as-current metric or alert.

attacks.claim: The request carries the visible map viewport (bbox) along with the client IP to an origin. That is a coarse location of the user, contradicting the claim that location is not sent. Request-log retention and linkage to devices are not specified.
attacks.evidence: "The app requests forecasts by zone id for the visible map tiles; device location is not sent." and "`GET /avy/v1/zones?bbox=…`" ABSENT: log retention period, IP truncation, or whether bbox is stored.

attacks.claim: The summary of the WADE agreement covers display only. It does not establish that storing forecast data on-device for offline use, or redistributing it through our CDN, is permitted. Those are core features of this release.
attacks.evidence: "display in our app is permitted for free and paid users" and "Offline: ... the current forecast for those zones is stored with it." ABSENT: agreement clause covering caching, storage, or CDN redistribution.

attacks.claim: The zone color is computed as the maximum of three band ratings, which is a derived rating. The artifact also says ratings are shown exactly as issued and never altered. Legal should confirm the derivation is allowed.
attacks.evidence: "The zone color uses the highest of the three" versus "We show the rating exactly as issued (1-5 plus name)."

attacks.claim: The analytics events tie tapped zone ids to a session or device identifier that is not described. Tapped backcountry zones can reveal where a user goes, so the "zone id only" claim does not establish unlinkability.
attacks.evidence: "Analytics adds two events (layer toggled, card opened) with zone id only, no location or account id." ABSENT: whether a device or session id is attached to these events.

attacks.claim: The bbox parameter has no stated size or zone-count cap. A very large bbox returns every zone in one response, which is a cheap way to load the origin with uncached queries.
attacks.evidence: "GET /avy/v1/zones?bbox=…" and "rate limited at origin to 120 req/min per IP (CDN-cached responses are not counted)" ABSENT: bbox size limit.

attacks.claim: The 1.8M requests/day projection has no stated user base. Only origin cost is budgeted, while CDN bandwidth and egress, which the $400 alert covers, have no estimate.
attacks.evidence: "Projected 1.8M zone requests/day at 92% CDN hit rate; origin cost ~$140/month." ABSENT: DAU assumption and CDN bandwidth estimate.

attacks.claim: The VoiceOver and TalkBack announcement format is given only for a live zone. Expired and no-forecast zones, which carry the safety state, have no specified announcement.
attacks.evidence: "zone announced as '[zone], danger 3 Considerable, issued [time]'" ABSENT: announcement for expired or 'No current forecast' zones.

attacks.claim: Times are shown in the card without a stated time zone, and expired and no-forecast states may be visually similar. A user reading an "issued" or "valid-until" time in another zone could misjudge freshness.
attacks.evidence: "the card shows ... the issue time, the valid-until time" ABSENT: time zone format. "gray hatched fill and 'No current forecast'" and "gray hatched 'Forecast expired [time]'" share the same fill.

attacks.claim: The blog copy says forecasts come from 19 centers, but QA showed out-of-season centers render 'No current forecast'. At launch, some of the 19 may show no forecast.
attacks.evidence: "Avalanche forecasts from 19 avalanche centers across the US and Canada, now in Ridgeline Maps." and "Out-of-season center (no forecast) ... gray hatched 'No current forecast'"

attacks.claim: The go-live check confirms only that all 19 centers render. It does not verify forecast freshness at the moment of publication, so the blog post can go live with stale or empty data for some centers.
attacks.evidence: "Blog post and in-app card go live at 10:00 after a check that all 19 centers render."

attacks.claim: Nit: the unauthenticated bbox endpoint has no stated input validation or maximum bbox area, so a single request can ask for an arbitrarily large region.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: validation or max-area limits for GET /avy/v1/zones?bbox=…

attacks.claim: Each forecast request sends a map-viewport bbox along with the client IP. Over time that links a device to where it looks in backcountry terrain, which contradicts the framing that location is not sent. Retention and access policy for these logs is not stated.
attacks.evidence: 'requests forecasts by zone id for the visible map tiles; device location is not sent' vs 'GET /avy/v1/zones?bbox=…'; ABSENT: log retention and access policy for endpoint request logs

attacks.claim: Nit: the layer depends entirely on one data source (WADE). The plan has no fallback if the agreement ends, and the hosting and CDN vendors are not named.
attacks.evidence: 'using forecasts published by the regional avalanche centers in the Western Avalanche Data Exchange (WADE)'; ABSENT: exit plan if C-2209 terminates

attacks.claim: The CDN cache key includes an arbitrary bbox, so varying bbox values cause cache misses that go to origin. Origin is capped at 6 instances, and the per-IP rate limit does not stop distributed traffic. Headroom at 10x load is not shown.
attacks.evidence: '1.8M zone requests/day at 92% CDN hit rate'; 'origin autoscaling capped at 6 instances'; ABSENT: load test, per-instance capacity, bbox quantization or cache-key normalization

attacks.claim: Nit: the $140/month figure covers origin only. No CDN cost projection is given, so it is unclear whether the $400 CDN alert will fire, and the alert has no cutoff behavior.
attacks.evidence: 'origin cost ~$140/month'; 'CDN budget alert at $400/month'; ABSENT: CDN cost projection and cutoff

attacks.claim: Nit: app behavior on endpoint 5xx or timeouts is unspecified. Shared NAT at ski huts or group sites can also hit the 120 req/min per-IP limit and throttle legitimate users.
attacks.evidence: 'rate limited at origin to 120 req/min per IP'; ABSENT: client behavior on 5xx and timeouts; no alert for all-zones-expired

attacks.claim: The rollback does not reach offline devices. Flag changes apply only on the next foreground and need network access, so a phone in the field with a cached flag=true keeps showing the layer and stored ratings. The timing also conflicts with QA, which says purge happens on next launch.
attacks.evidence: 'takes effect on next app foreground' and 'on-device forecast data ... is deleted, so no stale ratings remain on phones' vs QA: 'offline forecast data purged on next launch'

attacks.claim: The offline expiry check only catches a device clock set earlier than the server download time. A clock that runs behind real time but stays after the download time keeps the forecast in color after valid_until has passed, which violates the agreed rule against presenting stale safety information as current. The QA test does not cover this case.
attacks.evidence: 'if the device clock reads earlier than that, the stored forecast is treated as expired'; QA: 'Device clock moved earlier than offline download time' only

attacks.claim: Nit: behavior is undefined when a forecast has a missing or unrated band, and when zone geometries from different centers overlap. Both affect which color is shown.
attacks.evidence: 'The zone color uses the highest of the three'; ABSENT: handling of unrated bands and overlapping zones

attacks.claim: Nit: QA rows lack dates, the centers that had active forecasts, and sample sizes. Today is 2026-10-26, so many centers may be out of season and the 3-day match may not have exercised active-forecast rendering for all 19.
attacks.evidence: 'All 19 centers: all three band ratings... match ... for 3 consecutive days | Pass, 0 mismatches'; ABSENT: dates and active-forecast coverage

attacks.claim: Nit: issue and expiry times are shown without a timezone, so 'Forecast expired [time]' can be read as local time when it refers to the center's time.
attacks.evidence: 'Forecast expired [time]'; 'issued [time]'

attacks.claim: Nit: the zone label shows only danger level, not issue or expiry time, so a user in the field must tap every zone to judge freshness.
attacks.evidence: 'each zone label also shows the number and name (e.g. "3 Considerable")'

attacks.claim: Nit: the 10:00 go-live depends on a manual check that all 19 centers render, which adds a two-hour gap after the flag turns on for everyone.
attacks.evidence: 'flag on for 100%' at 08:00; 'Blog post and in-app card go live at 10:00 after a check'

attacks.claim: Nit: contrast of the legend and of the gray hatched fill against the dark map style is not stated, although color-vision and VoiceOver were tested.
attacks.evidence: 'dark map style: labels legible'; ABSENT: contrast ratios for legend and hatched fill

attacks.claim: The public blog post and store notes are not covered by legal review (LGL-902 covers the card and terms only). The blog states the forecasts as a feature without the card's 'make your own assessment' caveat. Also, removing a center leaves its ratings visible offline until valid_until, which may not satisfy the agreement's withdrawal obligations.
attacks.evidence: 'Card text and the terms-of-use update were reviewed by legal (LGL-902)'; blog: 'Avalanche forecasts from 19 avalanche centers ... Free for everyone.'; 'any offline copies expire at their valid_until'

attacks.claim: Nit: the center list is duplicated in config and the blog post, and expiry logic is duplicated on server and device, so both can drift.
attacks.evidence: 'list in config/avy_centers.json, same list in the blog post'

attacks.claim: Nit: App Review notes say the review build had the layer enabled, but the public store notes omit it. Confirm the review notes match what ships.
attacks.evidence: 'App Review notes for 6.12 describe the layer and the remote flag, and the review build had it enabled'; 'public store notes do not mention the layer yet'
